blocks.text: A buildspec describes commands and artifacts in YAML. Version 0.2 supports commands in the same shell environment.
Put supplied commands in commands lists under needed phases, such as install, pre_build, build and post_build.
Match artifacts.files and, when needed, base-directory to generated output. Inspect phase logs and the exported artifact.

left.code:
cat <<'YAML'
version: 0.2
phases:
  build:
    commands:
      - mkdir -p dist
      - cp supplied-release.txt dist/release.txt
artifacts:
  base-directory: dist
  files: [release.txt]
YAML

tiles.title: Configure and verify an EC2 Auto Scaling policy under bounded load
tiles.summary: Compare metric, activities and capacity within approved bounds; above-target load cannot override the maximum.

steps.title: Configure and verify an EC2 Auto Scaling policy under bounded load

blocks.text: Target tracking adjusts Auto Scaling capacity to keep a chosen metric near its target.
Choose the approved metric and target; configure instance warmup and minimum, desired and maximum capacities.
During the bounded load test, compare metric values, scaling activities and resulting capacity. Capacity cannot exceed the configured maximum.

In the supplied timeline, read metric values alongside activities and capacity. At the maximum, an above-target metric is not permission to exceed the bound. These authored observations are not exact response-time guarantees.

blocks.alt_text: Two aligned panels show the fictional bounded-test timeline. CPU utilization rises above the approved target while capacity increases from its starting desired capacity to the configured maximum. CPU remains above target at the maximum; capacity does not exceed that bound. The lower panel labels scale-out activities and the maximum-capacity observation, minimum and maximum bounds and the starting desired capacity; the footer states the supplied instance warmup. These are authored observations, not exact response-time guarantees.

blocks.text: CloudWatch log-group retention controls how long events remain. By default, logs are retained indefinitely.

blocks.text: terraform validate checks syntax and internal consistency, not remote service state or provider API success.
Where backend access is unnecessary, initialize needed providers and modules with terraform init -backend=false before static validation.
Make terraform validate blocking. Stop on nonzero exit, correct the invalid declaration and rerun before the supplied approved apply step.
terraform fmt -check checks canonical formatting and can serve as an additional blocking configuration check.

For the supplied invalid EC2 declaration, validation failure must block apply. After correction, rerun validation and any blocking formatting check. A formatting-only change is not a configuration-validity correction, and static-check success is not provisioning evidence.
